messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Canary cluster canary-asia-2 (deploy: model-v14-timewarp) p95 and p99 latency spike detected across streaming endpoints. p95 -> 420ms (baseline 95ms), p99 -> 1.9s (baseline 360ms). Error rate low, but streaming stalls observed (~0.7% stall/early-close). Dashboard: https://dashboards.internal/redwood/canary-asia-2/query?range=15m :rotating_light:
samir (oncall-sre): acked. getting logs now. paging to oncall. paging: @samir @elaine @jia :phone:  

samir (oncall-sre): quick check: are we seeing KV cache evictions? query shows kvcache.evictions spike coincident with deploy. possible cache index mismatch after v14 change. 

elaine (infra): confirmed host-level metrics show CPU steady, networking normal. GPUs not saturated. KV-tier-2 eviction rate + write amplification up. Could be new attention cache layout. 

jia (runtime): rolling change in v14 introduces a different kv-key schema for streaming prefix caching (fastpath flag). Clients hitting mixed pool might miss cached prefixes -> more cold KV reads -> tail latency. Repro steps on bench look similar. Recommend immediate mitigations: 1) shift traffic off canary, 2) toggle fastpath flag off for v14, or 3) rollback v14. 

ash (platform): can do a traffic shift to baseline-model-compat (v13-compat) across canary-asia-2 to drain v14. propose 40% -> 10% -> 0% in 3m intervals. want quick confirmation to run. 

samir (oncall-sre): go for the traffic shift now. need an immediate mitigation before a full rollback. run step and observe p99. 

ops-bot: executing routing change: curl -X POST https://router.internal/api/shift -d '{"cluster":"canary-asia-2","from":"model-v14-timewarp","to":"model-v13-compat","steps":[{"pct":40,"delay_s":60},{"pct":10,"delay_s":120},{"pct":0,"delay_s":180}]}' --header "Authorization: Bearer {{ROUTER_TOKEN}}"  

ops-bot: routing change accepted. job id: rjob-7829. monitoring p99 across streaming routes. 

samir (oncall-sre): watching p95/p99. initial drop p95 -> 180ms, p99 -> 900ms. still above baseline but much better. continue. 

jia (runtime): while shift executes, start validating fastpath toggle rollback: set FASTPATH=false for v14 replicas. config change command below if we decide to toggle rather than full rollback:  

```bash
# toggle fastpath for canary pool
redwoodctl set-config --pool canary-asia-2 --model model-v14-timewarp --env FASTPATH=false
``` 

elaine (infra): note: toggling will keep v14 serving but may cause some in-flight sessions to reconnect/lose cache. customers with long streaming sessions might see reconnects. weigh against full rollback which is heavier but cleaner. 

customer-ops: heads up: we have alerts for 2 paying customers, AcmePayments and NimbusHealth, showing elevated response latency and a handful of aborted streaming sessions. contacting them to set expectations. no confirmed customer-facing errors yet but degraded QoS. 

samir (oncall-sre): rjob-7829 reports final step done. canary-asia-2 now at 0% v14. p95 now 110ms, p99 320ms. streaming stalls reduced to ~0.06%. marking live mitigation success. :tada: 

jia (runtime): good. we should still collect heap/kv snapshots from v14 pods before tearing them down. add a quick postmortem data capture:  

```text
kubectl exec -n canary canary-v14-abc -- /bin/sh -c 'tar czf /tmp/v14-kv-snapshot.tar.gz /var/lib/kv/* && scp /tmp/v14-kv-snapshot.tar.gz logs@storage:/artifacts/canary-v14/3894507777/'
``` 

ash (platform): I'll coordinate artifact retrieval and tag the deployment for rollback-audit. also creating a ticket for rollout gating — looks like fastpath should be behind stricter compatibility checks for kv schema. 

elaine (infra): quick customer impact note: AcmePayments saw 5 aborted streams in last 20m, NimbusHealth saw 2. both on canary-asia-2, both on streaming-large payloads. advise Customer Success to send a short note saying we mitigated and will follow up. 

customer-ops: sending now to both customers. template: "We observed degraded streaming performance in a canary rollout (model-v14). We've rolled the traffic back and are investigating. We'll share a follow-up with root cause and timeline." 

samir (oncall-sre): creating incident tracker: INC-2026-canary-timewarp-p99. assigning SRE/jia/infra. immediate action: postmortem capture + reproduce on bench + tighter rollout gating. 

ops-bot: incident INC-2026 created by @samir. incident channel: #inc-2026-canary-timewarp. 

samir (oncall-sre): follow-ups: 1) Jia to produce a short RCA on kv schema difference and why fallback didn't trigger. 2) Platform to add automated schema-compat test in rollout pipeline. 3) Infra to update runbook for fastpath toggles and side-effects. 4) CS to notify customers.  

jia (runtime): already started bench reproducer. initial hypothesis: v14 changed kv namespace prefix to include model version token; mixed traffic hit both and got cache misses. patch options: backfill compatibility layer or keep fastpath off until schema migration tool runs. 

elaine (infra): adding runbook note: if p99 > 1s with KV eviction spike and errors low -> prefer traffic shift over immediate rollback unless customers are erroring. 

ash (platform): assigning follow-up tickets: PLT-908 (gating tests), PLT-909 (routing automation tweaks), PLT-910 (rollout audit). 

samir (oncall-sre): closing thread for live mitigation; will update incident channel INC-2026 with full timeline and next steps. thanks all. :raised_hands:

ops-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated -> monitoring. priority: P2.

samir (oncall-sre): postmortem owner: @jia. ETA for draft: 24h.
